sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca hanta te kathayiṣyāmi nītim āpatsu bhārata utsṛjyāpi ghṛṇāṃ kāle yathā varteta bhūmipaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Listen, O descendant of Bharata, and I shall expound to you the polity for times of calamity—how, when the hour demands it, a king should conduct himself, even setting compassion aside.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam bharadvājasya saṃvādaṃ rājñaḥ śatruṃtapasya ca
english: On this they recite an ancient tale: the colloquy between Bharadvāja and the king Śatruṃtapa.

sanskrit: rājā śatruṃtapo nāma sauvīrāṇāṃ mahārathaḥ kaṇiṅkam upasaṃgamya papracchārthaviniścayam
english: A king named Śatruṃtapa, a great chariot-warrior of the Sauvīras, approached Kaṇiṅka and asked him for a clear ruling on policy.

sanskrit: alabdhasya kathaṃ lipsā labdhaṃ kena vivardhate vardhitaṃ pālayet kena pālitaṃ praṇayet katham
english: How is one to win what has not yet been won? By what means is the won made to grow? How should one guard what has grown, and how dispense what has been guarded?

sanskrit: tasmai viniścayārthaṃ sa paripṛṣṭārthaniścayaḥ uvāca brāhmaṇo vākyam idaṃ hetumad uttaram
english: Thus questioned for a settled ruling, the brāhmaṇa, whose own conclusions were firm, made this reasoned reply to him.

sanskrit: nityam udyatadaṇḍaḥ syān nityaṃ vivṛtapauruṣaḥ acchidraś chidradarśī ca pareṣāṃ vivarānugaḥ
english: Let him keep the rod ever uplifted and his prowess ever displayed; let him be without any flaw himself yet sharp to detect flaws, and quick to seize upon the openings of his foes.

sanskrit: nityam udyatadaṇḍasya bhṛśam udvijate janaḥ tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni daṇḍenaiva prarodhayet
english: Before one whose rod is always raised the people tremble greatly; therefore by the rod alone should he hold all creatures in check.

sanskrit: evam eva praśaṃsanti paṇḍitās tattvadarśinaḥ tasmāc catuṣṭaye tasmin pradhāno daṇḍa ucyate
english: Just so do the wise who perceive the truth give their praise; therefore, of those four expedients, the rod is declared the chief.

sanskrit: chinnamūle hy adhiṣṭhāne sarve tajjīvino hatāḥ kathaṃ hi śākhās tiṣṭheyuś chinnamūle vanaspatau
english: When the foundation is cut at the root, all who lived upon it are undone; for how should the branches stand when the great tree is severed at its root?

sanskrit: mūlam evāditaś chindyāt parapakṣasya paṇḍitaḥ tataḥ sahāyān pakṣaṃ ca sarvam evānusārayet
english: The wise man should first of all cut down the very root of the rival party, and thereafter pursue its allies and its whole faction without exception.

sanskrit: sumantritaṃ suvikrāntaṃ suyuddhaṃ supalāyitam āpadāṃ padakāleṣu kurvīta na vicārayet
english: Well-counselled, well-charged, well-fought, well-fled—at the very moments when calamities arise let him so act, and not hesitate.

sanskrit: vāṅmātreṇa vinītaḥ syād dhṛdayena yathā kṣuraḥ ślakṣṇapūrvābhibhāṣī ca kāmakrodhau vivarjayet
english: In speech alone let him seem all modesty, while at heart he is keen as a razor; let his words be smooth and gentle from the outset, and let him put away both lust and wrath.

sanskrit: sapatnasahite kārye kṛtvā saṃdhiṃ na viśvaset apakrāmet tataḥ kṣipraṃ kṛtakāryo vicakṣaṇaḥ
english: In any affair that involves a rival, the discerning man, though he has made a treaty, should not trust it; rather, his purpose once accomplished, let him withdraw at once.

sanskrit: śatruṃ ca mitrarūpeṇa sāntvenaivābhisāntvayet nityaśaś codvijet tasmāt sarpād veśmagatād iva
english: Wearing the guise of a friend, he should appease his enemy with conciliating words, yet shrink from him perpetually, as from a serpent that has crept into the house.

sanskrit: yasya buddhiṃ paribhavet tam atītena sāntvayet anāgatena duṣprajñaṃ pratyutpannena paṇḍitam
english: Him whose mind he would outwit, the dull-witted let him pacify with what is past or with what is yet to come; the shrewd, with what is present at hand.

sanskrit: añjaliṃ śapathaṃ sāntvaṃ praṇamya śirasā vadet aśruprapātanaṃ caiva kartavyaṃ bhūtim icchatā
english: Folded hands, an oath, soft words, the bowing of the head in speech, and even the shedding of tears—all this must he who desires prosperity be ready to perform.

sanskrit: vahed amitraṃ skandhena yāvat kālaviparyayaḥ athainam āgate kāle bhindyād ghaṭam ivāśmani
english: Let him carry his foe upon his very shoulder so long as the time runs adverse; but when the hour has come, let him dash him to pieces as one shatters a pot upon a stone.

sanskrit: muhūrtam api rājendra tindukālātavaj jvalet na tuṣāgnir ivānarcir dhūmāyeta naraś ciram
english: Better, O lord of kings, that a man blaze for even a single moment like a brand of tinduka wood, than that he smoulder long, flameless, like a fire of chaff.

sanskrit: nānarthakenārthavattvaṃ kṛtaghnena samācaret arthe tu śakyate bhoktuṃ kṛtakāryo 'vamanyate tasmāt sarvāṇi kāryāṇi sāvaśeṣāṇi kārayet
english: With a useless or an ungrateful man one should not pursue a profitable end; yet so long as the gain may still be enjoyed, the ingrate may be used—for once his purpose is fulfilled, he scorns his helper. Therefore let him conduct all his affairs in such a way that something still remains undone.

sanskrit: kokilasya varāhasya meroḥ śūnyasya veśmanaḥ vyāḍasya bhakticitrasya yac chreṣṭhaṃ tat samācaret
english: Whatever is best in the cuckoo, the boar, Mount Meru, an empty house, the serpent, and the dappled deer—that let him take to himself and practise.

sanskrit: utthāyotthāya gacchec ca nityayukto ripor gṛhān kuśalaṃ cāpi pṛccheta yady apy akuśalaṃ bhavet
english: Rising again and again, ever attentive, let him go to the houses of his foe and inquire after his welfare, even when he wishes him ill.

sanskrit: nālasāḥ prāpnuvanty arthān na klībā na ca māninaḥ na ca lokaravād bhītā na ca śaśvat pratīkṣiṇaḥ
english: The slothful do not gain their ends, nor do the weaklings, nor the overproud, nor those who dread the gossip of the world, nor those who are forever biding their time.

sanskrit: nāsya chidraṃ paro vidyād vidyāc chidraṃ parasya tu gūhet kūrma ivāṅgāni rakṣed vivaram ātmanaḥ
english: Let no enemy discern a flaw in him, while he discerns the flaw in the enemy; let him draw in his limbs like a tortoise and guard his own vulnerable point.

sanskrit: bakavac cintayed arthān siṃhavac ca parākramet vṛkavac cāvalumpeta śaśavac ca viniṣpatet
english: Let him plot his ends like a heron, charge like a lion, snatch like a wolf, and break away like a hare.

sanskrit: pānam akṣās tathā nāryo mṛgayā gītavāditam etāni yuktyā seveta prasaṅgo hy atra doṣavān
english: Drink, dice, women, the hunt, song and music—these let him enjoy with measure, for excessive attachment to them is fraught with ruin.

sanskrit: kuryāt tṛṇamayaṃ cāpaṃ śayīta mṛgaśāyikām andhaḥ syād andhavelāyāṃ bādhiryam api saṃśrayet
english: He may make himself a bow of straw and lie down in a deer's posture; in a time for blindness let him be blind, and may even take refuge in deafness.

sanskrit: deśaṃ kālaṃ samāsādya vikrameta vicakṣaṇaḥ deśakālābhyatīto hi vikramo niṣphalo bhavet
english: Having met with the right place and the right time, let the discerning man exert his valour; for valour that has overshot place and time bears no fruit.

sanskrit: kālākālau saṃpradhārya balābalam athātmanaḥ parasparabalaṃ jñātvā tathātmānaṃ niyojayet
english: Weighing the seasonable and the unseasonable, his own strength and weakness, and knowing too the relative strength of the two sides, let him then direct himself accordingly.

sanskrit: daṇḍenopanataṃ śatruṃ yo rājā na niyacchati sa mṛtyum upagūhyās te garbham aśvatarī yathā
english: The king who, having brought his enemy low by the rod, does not then subdue him, embraces his own death—as a she-mule conceiving a foal embraces hers.

sanskrit: supuṣpitaḥ syād aphalaḥ phalavān syād durāruhaḥ āmaḥ syāt pakvasaṃkāśo na ca śīryeta kasya cit
english: Let him be full of blossom yet bear no fruit; or fruitful, yet hard to climb; let him be unripe though seeming ripe, and never let himself crumble away to anyone.

sanskrit: āśāṃ kālavatīṃ kuryāt tāṃ ca vighnena yojayet vighnaṃ nimittato brūyān nimittaṃ cāpi hetutaḥ
english: Let him hold out a hope tied to a future time, and then couple that hope with an obstacle; let him ascribe the obstacle to some pretext, and the pretext, in turn, to some cause.

sanskrit: bhītavat saṃvidhātavyaṃ yāvad bhayam anāgatam āgataṃ tu bhayaṃ dṛṣṭvā prahartavyam abhītavat
english: So long as the danger has not yet come, let him make his arrangements like one who is afraid; but seeing the danger actually arrived, let him strike like one who fears nothing.

sanskrit: na saṃśayam anāruhya naro bhadrāṇi paśyati saṃśayaṃ punar āruhya yadi jīvati paśyati
english: Without venturing into risk a man beholds no good fortune; but having ventured into risk, if he survives, he beholds it.

sanskrit: anāgataṃ vijānīyād yacched bhayam upasthitam punar vṛddhikṣayāt kiṃ cid abhivṛttaṃ niśāmayet
english: Let him foresee what has not yet come, and ward off the danger that is at hand; and from the rise and fall of things let him discern whatever may already have come to pass.

sanskrit: pratyupasthitakālasya sukhasya parivarjanam anāgatasukhāśā ca naiṣa buddhimatāṃ nayaḥ
english: To forsake the happiness whose hour is present, and to hanker after a happiness yet to come—this is no policy of the wise.

sanskrit: yo 'riṇā saha saṃdhāya sukhaṃ svapiti viśvasan sa vṛkṣāgraprasupto vā patitaḥ pratibudhyate
english: He who, having made a pact with his enemy, sleeps in trustful ease, awakens only when he has fallen—like one who has dozed off at the top of a tree.

sanskrit: karmaṇā yena teneha mṛdunā dāruṇena vā uddhared dīnam ātmānaṃ samartho dharmam ācaret
english: By whatever deed serves—be it gentle or be it harsh—let him lift up his own afflicted self; and once he is strong again, let him practise dharma.

sanskrit: ye sapatnāḥ sapatnānāṃ sarvāṃs tān apavatsayet ātmanaś cāpi boddhavyāś cārāḥ praṇihitāḥ paraiḥ
english: Whoever are the rivals of his rivals, all of these let him win over to himself; and let him also be alert to the spies set upon him by his foes.

sanskrit: cāraḥ suvihitaḥ kārya ātmano 'tha parasya ca pāṣaṇḍāṃs tāpasādīṃś ca pararāṣṭraṃ praveśayet
english: Espionage must be well organized, both for his own realm and against the other's; and let him send heretics, ascetics, and the like into the enemy's kingdom.

sanskrit: udyāneṣu vihāreṣu prapāsv āvasatheṣu ca pānāgāreṣu veśeṣu tīrtheṣu ca sabhāsu ca
english: In gardens and pleasure-grounds, at watering-sheds and lodging-houses, in taverns and brothels, at sacred fords and in assembly-halls—

sanskrit: dharmābhicāriṇaḥ pāpāś cārā lokasya kaṇṭakāḥ samāgacchanti tān buddhvā niyacchec chamayed api
english: —there sinful men who transgress dharma, the spies and thorns of society, congregate; discovering them, let him restrain them, and even put them down.

sanskrit: na viśvased aviśvaste viśvaste nāpi viśvaset viśvastaṃ bhayam anveti nāparīkṣya ca viśvaset
english: Let him not trust the untrustworthy, nor yet trust even the trustworthy; for danger pursues the trusting man, and let him never trust without first putting to the test.

sanskrit: viśvāsayitvā tu paraṃ tattvabhūtena hetunā athāsya praharet kāle kiṃ cid vicalite pade
english: Having won his adversary's confidence by some genuine-seeming pretext, then, when the moment comes and his footing is even a little unsteady, let him strike him down.

sanskrit: aśaṅkyam api śaṅketa nityaṃ śaṅketa śaṅkitāt bhayaṃ hi śaṅkitāj jātaṃ samūlam api kṛntati
english: Let him be suspicious even of what seems beyond suspicion, and ever wary of one already suspected; for danger born of one suspected can cut a man down, root and all.

sanskrit: avadhānena maunena kāṣāyeṇa jaṭājinaiḥ viśvāsayitvā dveṣṭāram avalumped yathā vṛkaḥ
english: By a show of devotion, by silence, by the ochre robe, by matted locks and the deerskin, let him win the trust of one who hates him, and then seize upon him as a wolf upon its prey.

sanskrit: putro vā yadi vā bhrātā pitā vā yadi vā suhṛt arthasya vighnaṃ kurvāṇā hantavyā bhūtivardhanāḥ
english: Be it a son, or a brother, or a father, or a bosom friend—if they stand in the way of his purpose, they are to be struck down by him who would increase his fortune.

sanskrit: guror apy avaliptasya kāryākāryam ajānataḥ utpathapratipannasya daṇḍo bhavati śāsanam
english: Even a teacher, if he is arrogant, ignorant of what should and should not be done, and gone astray upon a wrong path—for him the rod becomes the fitting discipline.

sanskrit: pratyutthānābhivādābhyāṃ saṃpradānena kasya cit pratipuṣkalaghātī syāt tīkṣṇatuṇḍa iva dvijaḥ
english: By rising to greet, by salutation, by gifts bestowed on this man or that, let him be a striker who deals abundant blows in return, like a sharp-beaked bird.

sanskrit: nācchittvā paramarmāṇi nākṛtvā karma dāruṇam nāhatvā matsyaghātīva prāpnoti paramāṃ śriyam
english: Without cutting into the vital points of others, without doing some terrible deed, without striking—as a fisherman slays his fish—a man wins no surpassing glory.

sanskrit: nāsti jātyā ripur nāma mitraṃ nāma na vidyate sāmarthyayogāj jāyante mitrāṇi ripavas tathā
english: None is by birth an enemy, and none, indeed, is by birth a friend; it is from the interplay of power that friends and foes alike arise.

sanskrit: amitraṃ naiva muñceta bruvantaṃ karuṇāny api duḥkhaṃ tatra na kurvīta hanyāt pūrvāpakāriṇam
english: Let him by no means release a foe, though he plead piteously; let him feel no pity in that, but slay the man who first did the wrong.

sanskrit: saṃgrahānugrahe yatnaḥ sadā kāryo 'nasūyatā nigrahaś cāpi yatnena kartavyo bhūtim icchatā
english: Effort, free of all spite, must ever be made in winning men over and showing them favour; and with equal effort must restraint and punishment be applied by him who desires prosperity.

sanskrit: prahariṣyan priyaṃ brūyāt prahṛtyāpi priyottaram api cāsya śiraś chittvā rudyāc choced athāpi vā
english: When about to strike, let him speak kindly, and even after striking let his words be kind; nay, having struck off his victim's head, let him weep and mourn for him.

sanskrit: nimantrayeta sāntvena saṃmānena titikṣayā āśākāraṇam ity etat kartavyaṃ bhūtim icchatā
english: Let him conciliate with soft words, with honour shown, with forbearance—this giving of grounds for hope is what he who desires prosperity must do.

sanskrit: na śuṣkavairaṃ kurvīta na bāhubhyāṃ nadīṃ taret apārthakam anāyuṣyaṃ goviṣāṇasya bhakṣaṇam dantāś ca parighṛṣyante rasaś cāpi na labhyate
english: Let him not engage in a fruitless feud, nor try to cross a river by the strength of his own arms alone; it is profitless and life-shortening—like gnawing on a cow's horn, wherein the teeth are merely worn away and no juice is got at all.

sanskrit: trivarge trividhā pīḍānubandhās traya eva ca anubandhavadhau jñātvā pīḍāṃ hi parivarjayet
english: In the threefold aim of life there are three kinds of affliction and three kinds of consequence; knowing the consequences and their undoing, let him shun the affliction.

sanskrit: ṛṇaśeṣo 'gniśeṣaś ca śatruśeṣas tathaiva ca punaḥ punar vivardheta svalpo 'py anivāritaḥ
english: A remnant of debt, a remnant of fire, and likewise a remnant of an enemy—each, however small, if left unchecked, will grow again and again.

sanskrit: vardhamānam ṛṇaṃ tiṣṭhat paribhūtāś ca śatravaḥ āvahanty anayaṃ tīvraṃ vyādhayaś cāpy upekṣitāḥ
english: A debt left to mount, enemies left despised, and ailments left neglected—these bring on grievous ruin.

sanskrit: nāsamyak kṛtakārī syād apramattaḥ sadā bhavet kaṇṭako 'pi hi duśchinno vikāraṃ kurute ciram
english: Let him not be one who does his work by halves; let him be ever vigilant—for even a thorn ill-extracted festers and causes trouble for a long time.

sanskrit: vadhena ca manuṣyāṇāṃ mārgāṇāṃ dūṣaṇena ca ākarāṇāṃ vināśaiś ca pararāṣṭraṃ vināśayet
english: By the slaying of its men, by the spoiling of its roads, and by the wrecking of its mines, let him bring the enemy's kingdom to ruin.

sanskrit: gṛdhradṛṣṭir bakālīnaḥ śvaceṣṭaḥ siṃhavikramaḥ anudvignaḥ kākaśaṅkī bhujaṃgacaritaṃ caret
english: With the eye of a vulture, the stillness of a heron, the wariness of a dog, the valour of a lion, untroubled yet suspicious as a crow, let him move with the gait of a serpent.

sanskrit: śreṇimukhyopajāpeṣu vallabhānunayeṣu ca amātyān parirakṣeta bhedasaṃghātayor api
english: When guild-chiefs are being suborned and favourites courted away, let him keep close watch over his ministers, both as to their dividing and their banding together.

sanskrit: mṛdur ity avamanyante tīkṣṇa ity udvijanti ca tīkṣṇakāle ca tīkṣṇaḥ syān mṛdukāle mṛdur bhavet
english: Men scorn him as soft, and shrink from him as harsh; therefore in a time for harshness let him be harsh, and in a time for gentleness let him be gentle.

sanskrit: mṛdunā sumṛduṃ hanti mṛdunā hanti dāruṇam nāsādhyaṃ mṛdunā kiṃ cit tasmāt tīkṣṇataraṃ mṛdu
english: By gentleness one overcomes the very gentle, and by gentleness one overcomes the fierce; there is nothing gentleness cannot accomplish—therefore gentleness is the keener weapon.

sanskrit: kāle mṛdur yo bhavati kāle bhavati dāruṇaḥ sa sādhayati kṛtyāni śatrūṃś caivādhitiṣṭhati
english: He who is gentle when the time is for gentleness and fierce when the time is for fierceness, he accomplishes his ends and prevails over his foes.

sanskrit: paṇḍitena viruddhaḥ san dūre 'smīti na viśvaset dīrghau buddhimato bāhū yābhyāṃ hiṃsati hiṃsitaḥ
english: Being at odds with a wise man, let him not trust in the thought, "I am far away"; for long are the arms of the intelligent, with which, once injured, he injures in return.

sanskrit: na tat tared yasya na pāram uttaren; na tad dhared yat punar āharet paraḥ na tat khaned yasya na mūlam utkhanen; na taṃ hanyād yasya śiro na pātayet
english: Let him not embark on what he cannot cross to the farther shore; let him not seize what the enemy can seize back again; let him not dig at what he cannot uproot; let him not strike at one whose head he cannot strike off.

sanskrit: itīdam uktaṃ vṛjinābhisaṃhitaṃ; na caitad evaṃ puruṣaḥ samācaret paraprayuktaṃ tu kathaṃ niśāmayed; ato mayoktaṃ bhavato hitārthinā
english: Thus has this counsel, bound up with crookedness, been spoken; yet a man should not himself act in this way. But how else is he to recognize such devices when an enemy employs them? It is for this that I, desiring your good, have told it to you.

sanskrit: yathāvad uktaṃ vacanaṃ hitaṃ tadā; niśamya vipreṇa suvīrarāṣṭriyaḥ tathākarod vākyam adīnacetanaḥ; śriyaṃ ca dīptāṃ bubhuje sabāndhavaḥ
english: Having heard this salutary counsel duly delivered by the brāhmaṇa, the lord of the Suvīra realm, undaunted in mind, acted upon it, and together with his kinsmen enjoyed a blazing prosperity.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca hīne paramake dharme sarvalokātilaṅghini adharme dharmatāṃ nīte dharme cādharmatāṃ gate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When the supreme dharma, which surpasses all the worlds, has decayed—when unrighteousness has been raised to the rank of righteousness, and righteousness has lapsed into unrighteousness—

sanskrit: maryādāsu prabhinnāsu kṣubhite dharmaniścaye rājabhiḥ pīḍite loke corair vāpi viśāṃ pate
english: —when all bounds are broken asunder and the very settled order of dharma is convulsed, when the world is oppressed by kings or by thieves, O lord of peoples—

sanskrit: sarvāśrameṣu mūḍheṣu karmasūpahateṣu ca kāmān mohāc ca lobhāc ca bhayaṃ paśyatsu bhārata
english: —when all the orders of life are bewildered and their proper rites overthrown, and men, from desire, delusion, and greed, behold only fear, O descendant of Bharata—

sanskrit: aviśvasteṣu sarveṣu nityabhīteṣu pārthiva nikṛtyā hanyamāneṣu vañcayatsu parasparam
english: —when all are distrustful and ever afraid, O king, when men are slain by treachery and deceive one another—

sanskrit: saṃpradīpteṣu deśeṣu brāhmaṇye cābhipīḍite avarṣati ca parjanye mitho bhede samutthite
english: —when the lands are ablaze and the order of brāhmaṇas is sorely afflicted, when the rain-cloud withholds its rain and mutual dissension has arisen—

sanskrit: sarvasmin dasyusād bhūte pṛthivyām upajīvane kena svid brāhmaṇo jīvej jaghanye kāla āgate
english: —when every means of livelihood upon the earth has fallen into the hands of brigands: by what means, then, is a brāhmaṇa to live, once so vile a time has come?

sanskrit: atityakṣuḥ putrapautrān anukrośān narādhipa katham āpatsu varteta tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: How, O ruler of men, should one who is unwilling to abandon his sons and grandsons out of compassion conduct himself in such calamities? This tell me, grandfather.

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca rājā varteta loke kaluṣatāṃ gate katham arthāc ca dharmāc ca na hīyeta paraṃtapa
english: And how should a king conduct himself when the world has fallen into turmoil? How, O scorcher of foes, is he to fall away neither from gain nor from dharma?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca rājamūlā mahārāja yogakṣemasuvṛṣṭayaḥ prajāsu vyādhayaś caiva maraṇaṃ ca bhayāni ca
english: Bhīṣma said: Rooted in the king, O great monarch, are security, prosperity, and good rains—and so too, among the people, are diseases, death, and the terrors that beset them.

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaś ca kaliś ca bharatarṣabha rājamūlāni sarvāṇi mama nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: The Kṛta age, the Tretā, the Dvāpara, and the Kali, O bull of the Bharatas—all of these are rooted in the king; of this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tv abhyāgate kāle prajānāṃ doṣakārake vijñānabalam āsthāya jīvitavyaṃ tadā bhavet
english: But when that time has come which works the undoing of the people, then one must live by taking one's stand upon the strength of discernment.
